claims.claim: Umeclidinium, a quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic, has negligible oral bioavailability and very low systemic exposure (13% absolute bioavailability overall, with oral contribution negligible).

Radiolabeled umeclidinium studies in healthy volunteers show systemic bioavailability of oral and inhaled drug ≤12%, with drug entering bloodstream principally through lung absorption from the inhaled route.
Umeclidinium has low oral bioavailability in healthy volunteers and very low oral bioavailability with inhaled formulation.
A related antimuscarinic ester, the (R)-enantiomer of oxybutynin, had an estimated oral bioavailability of 0.0669, consistent with low oral F for this ester/antimuscarinic class.

The query is a permanently charged quaternary ammonium tropane ester with an epoxide, sharing the key charge/class liability of umeclidinium; no supplied evidence indicates oral F ≥ 20% for this class.

evidence_gaps: No query-specific measured oral bioavailability or PK data are supplied.
Umeclidinium data are primarily from inhaled delivery; oral bioavailability is described as negligible/low but not a precise F value for the query.
No formulation, dose, or species match for the query is available.
No direct permeability or solubility measurements for the query are supplied; the prior is physicochemical only.
Metabolic lability of the ester/epoxide is not directly assessed.
content.decision_summary: Predicted low because the query is a permanently charged quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic; transferable direct evidence from umeclidinium (also a quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic) shows negligible/low oral bioavailability (≤12% systemic, largely via inhalation), and no affirmative evidence supports F ≥ 20%. Confidence is moderate due to lack of query-specific PK data.
